notes: Sworn on Ethereum mainnet, as specified by the approved workflow and docs/V3.md. Deploy Renderer, Composer, then Registry. Renderer draws the card and metadata on-chain; Composer composes oracle questions, validates community specs and reads direct traits. Both have no constructor arguments. Registry is the ownerless Sworn/SWORN ERC-721 registry: one transferable card per wallet, with facts bound to the minting wallet. Its seven address arguments follow the accepted constructor and ABI: curator (WhitelistCurator), imd (existing IMD token), intake (Intake v2), attester (the named IMD oracle signer), renderer, composer, burnExecutor (IMD BurnExecutor V2). All five external addresses are the approved mainnet values; both application references point to earlier deployments. IdentityMD is not a constructor dependency. These contracts grant no owner or admin role, so no $owner argument is needed. Mint and registration fees are forwarded to the BurnExecutor for bridging and burning on Base; oracle requests are paid by claimants through Intake. Deployment uses nonpayable constructors with no initialization calls. Blocking constructor/rehearsal finding: Registry always requires code at Renderer, Composer and BurnExecutor, and a nonzero attester. It skips only the Curator settlement, IMD decimals and Intake price reads when those three external read dependencies all lack code. The supplied protected probe deploys only the three applications on an otherwise empty chain, so the approved external BurnExecutor has no code and Registry reverts ExecutorHasNoCode. The existing FloorTest supplies executor code and therefore does not prove that protected probe passes. This conflict requires independent review and resolution in the constructor or deployment rehearsal; a manifest-only change cannot resolve it while preserving the accepted implementation and approved addresses. Source publication, signed artifact linkage, policy admission and deployment simulation belong to the services; this manifest does not assert that those checks have passed.
